static_traits.name: Zhao Kailin
static_traits.family_status: Living with spouse and three children
static_traits.social_status: Has some friends, but finds it hard to open up about fears and anxiety regarding the children
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; never had similar psychological issues before, never received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative; self-reported nervousness and anxiety; thinking dominated by worrying about the future, tending toward catastrophizing, predicting the future and black-and-white thinking; able to reflect but hard to see other possibilities

basic_info.main_problem: I have been struggling with fear about the children growing up, moving out and forgetting me, which makes me feel sad and anxious.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings have already affected my daily life and relationships with family; also hope that as the children grow, to find new ways of connecting.
growth_experiences: Since the youngest child started school and became more independent, my fear and unease have increased significantly: whenever I see the children reaching new milestones or showing stronger self-care ability, I am flooded by the thought that 'they will forget me when they grow up', with strong sadness and anxiety; afterwards I tried distracting with work and hobbies, but with poor results.

core_beliefs: I will be forgotten and abandoned by the children
If I am not needed, I have no value

special_situations.event: The youngest child has started school and become more independent
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the children become more independent, it means they no longer need me and will eventually forget me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Distracting by throwing oneself into work and hobbies, trying to control and ease anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One day they will forget me and I will be left alone

special_situations.event: Whenever the child reaches a new milestone or shows stronger self-care ability
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The more self-sufficient the child, the more our intimate bond will fade
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to arrange more parent-child interaction, for example planning a weekly family activity, in order to maintain the relationship
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Our connection is disappearing bit by bit; they no longer need me

special_situations.event: Thinking of the children moving out to live independently in the future
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The children leaving home equals no longer needing me, and treating me as nonexistent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly worries and rehearses the worst outcome, avoids discussing this topic with friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Once they leave, my existence will no longer matter to them

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be continuously needed and attached to by her child, maintaining a close and stable mother-child bond
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being abandoned and forgotten, worrying about losing self-worth once not needed
defense_goal: Maintains vigilance and a sense of control through persistent worry and reality rehearsal to avoid losing connection
Buffering anxiety and maintaining the feeling of being needed through distraction and arranging more interactions

object_relations.self_representation: A forgotten mother/caregiver who may be abandoned
object_relations.object_representation: Will move away, become cold, and eventually neglect her child (significant other)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to do reality testing or raises exploring 'whether there might be other outcomes', or discusses the topic of the children gradually becoming independent
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets the child's independence as an inevitable breakdown of the relationship, and believes others (including the counselor) underestimate her worries
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insisting on assertive statements like 'this is inevitable' and 'they will not need me in the future', tone anxious but firm; avoiding more careful evidence discussion and emotional deep-dives.

manifestations: Fearing the children will move out when grown and treat her as nonexistent
Equates children's independence with being abandoned, worrying about losing close connection
Strongly binding self-worth to 'being needed by the children', worrying about losing worth if not needed
outcomes: Pessimistic inferences about the future causing emotional distress

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Finding it hard to open up with friends about fears and anxiety regarding the children
Repeatedly scrutinizes and rehearses the worst possibilities inwardly, limiting genuine expression of needs

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Distracting oneself through work and hobbies, avoiding directly facing the fear of one's children growing up and becoming independent
Displacing the topic or staying busy with actions to avoid when strong emotions arise

exception_events.target_problem: When the children gradually become independent or reach milestones, the client usually develops strong anticipatory anxiety and sadness, believing the children will eventually forget her, thus affecting sleep, appetite and work performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At certain moments, the children still proactively seek her help or ask her advice, making her feel needed and valued, with anxiety eased and experiences of relief and joy.
exception_events.reason: Different support: the children's proactive interaction provided real evidence of the relationship; different understanding: focusing on actual connection in the present rather than a hypothetical worst future, so emotions were more eased this time.

positive_force: There are still genuine interactions and moments of being needed with the children
Willing to take concrete actions to maintain connection (such as planning family activities)
Willing to seek professional help and try new methods
negative_force: Cognitive distortions like catastrophizing, predicting the future and black-and-white thinking
Over-binds self-worth to 'being needed by the children'
Difficulty opening up to friends, insufficient use of social support
Persistent worry causing affected sleep and appetite, further lowering daily functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Anticipatory anxiety and sadness around the children leaving home in the future and no longer needing her
antecedent: The youngest child has started school and become more independent
The children reach milestones or show more self-care ability
Thinking of the children moving out to live independently in the future
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being abandoned and forgotten, strongly binding self-worth to 'being needed by the children', driven by cognitive biases like catastrophizing, predicting the future and black-and-white thinking
target_behavior.function: Seeking control and prevention through persistent worry, escaping direct experience of loneliness and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, affected sleep and appetite; relationship tension with spouse; difficulty opening up to friends socially
